quote: Yeah. Looks like we were supposed to meet with you about a month ago. We just weren't able to.
stewart_read: The rep surfaces that Ion missed a prior appointment with this customer a month ago but doesn't ask why it fell through or what was discussed, losing potential context on how the lead has been handled.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the miss irrelevant since the call topic itself shifted (customer wants a battery, not a new design), making the probe less valuable here.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly note what happened on the missed appointment for the record, even in a reschedule-only call, so recurring no-shows or routing errors are visible to management.

quote: No. The thing is the person said that, you guys have a Delta solar panel for me to take a look at. But I was saying I already have solar panel. All I needed was, like, batteries.
stewart_read: This is an orphaned-flow-adjacent scenario (existing solar owner requesting battery-only add-on) that the standard new-install script doesn't map to cleanly, but the rep didn't run any orphaned_flow qualifiers (who installed it, is it owned outright, is it working) before scheduling.
alternative_hypothesis: Since the appointment is purely to discuss batteries, the rep may be leaving that qualification to the specialist at the appointment itself, which is a legitimate scope-discipline call.
coaching_implication: Flag for the manager: confirm with Kenny whether battery-only leads on existing-solar homes require any setter-level qualification (system ownership, working status) before booking, since none of that was captured here.

quote: let me look at yeah. It says it's just for a battery. That's just a generic text that goes out.
stewart_read: Rep confirms the battery-only interest but does not ask any follow-up about why she wants a battery (backup power, outages, EV, etc.), missing a chance to anchor curiosity or urgency for the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the short, transactional nature of this reschedule call, the rep may have reasonably deferred the interest-reason conversation to the actual appointment.
coaching_implication: Encourage a single follow-up question here ("what's driving the interest in a battery?") — costs seconds and gives the closer a stronger opening.

quote: going out to a wedding tomorrow. I'll just sit.
stewart_read: Customer discloses she'll be traveling and unavailable until Tuesday; this is a scheduling-relevant detail the rep needed to track across the negotiation, and did track since the rep pursued Tuesday next.
coaching_implication: No action needed — rep correctly used this detail to move the negotiation forward to Tuesday.

stewart_read: Rep offers 10am without first confirming her full daily schedule, leading to an immediate correction from the customer about her commute time.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: the rep is guessing at open slots without having gathered the customer's full constraints upfront, causing avoidable back-and-forth. Strategic read is not well supported — there's no evidence the rep was deliberately testing options.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask an open question first ("what does your weekday schedule look like, start and end time?") rather than proposing individual slots and iterating by trial and error.

quote: So we could just do next Saturday. I know that's pretty far out, but we could do that.
stewart_read: Rep proposes the Saturday slot but frames it apologetically ("I know that's pretty far out") rather than confidently anchoring it as the right fit, which slightly undercuts the booking's firmness even though a time was ultimately locked.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as appropriate transparency/rapport rather than a weakness, since the customer readily agreed anyway.
coaching_implication: Encourage confident framing when offering a next available slot — state it as the good option, not an apology, to reinforce the appointment's importance.

quote: I'll shoot you a text so you have it in writing. Okay?
stewart_read: Rep closes with the required text-confirmation promise, meeting the button_up standard for follow-through, though there is no explicit recap of the appointment's purpose (battery discussion) or an "is that fair" handshake beyond the customer's agreement.
coaching_implication: Good habit to reinforce — but pair it going forward with a one-line recap of what the appointment covers (batteries) to make the confirmation text easy to personalize per text_after_call.tieback_to_interests_or_concerns.
